name: One King Down
label: Equal Vision
lede: An Albany straight edge band with a bassist on the Equal Vision payroll, a guitarist who auditioned for the Foo Fighters and three singers in five years, whose 1997 EP still outranks everything around it.

eras.title: Albany, before the growl
eras.text: One King Down started in Albany, New York around the Scoville brothers, playing crunchy, metallic hardcore in the mould of Snapcase and Earth Crisis. Their first singer made one CD and was gone before anyone outside upstate New York had heard of them.

years.p: Brothers Bill Scoville (bass) and Mike Scoville (guitar), guitarist Matt Wood, drummer Derrick Van Wie and original singer Bill Brown self-release the Jawbreaker demo cassette in Albany.

years.h: Absolve: One King Down's first CD, sung by Bill Brown
years.p: Trainwreck Records issues Absolve, four songs including Nine Eyes and The Killing Fields, with Bill Brown on vocals and Paul Benedetti engineering.
years.xp: Discogs credits Brown as the voice on Absolve; Wikipedia lists him as a former vocalist without naming him in its history. Equal Vision later tacked all four Absolve songs onto the CD of Gravity Wins Again in 2000.

years.h: Rob Fusco replaces Bill Brown as One King Down's singer
years.p: Rob Fusco takes over the mic. His growl and his vegan straight edge lyrics make One King Down a name well beyond Albany, though not everyone in the band goes vegan.
years.xp: Fusco dated his time in the band to 1995–1998 and 1999–2001 in a 2008 Lambgoat interview. Wikipedia notes the whole band was drug-free, but only some members were vegan.

eras.title: Bloodlust Revenge
eras.text: With Rob Fusco out front and an inside line to Equal Vision, where Bill Scoville worked for years, One King Down made the record people still judge them by. Then they got in the van with Hatebreed, Earth Crisis and Sick of It All.

years.p: Six songs built on Rob Fusco's vegan straight edge lyrics. It sold thousands at shows, and Wikipedia says most fans still rate it the band's finest recorded hour.
years.xp: Punknews later called it a six-song hardcore opus with nary a bad track. Its themes, mass drug use and a society too apathetic to help itself, carried the 20th-anniversary reissue two decades later.

years.h: One King Down tour with Hatebreed, Earth Crisis, VOD and Sick of It All
years.p: After Bloodlust Revenge, One King Down tour internationally with [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]], [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]], [[Vision of Disorder|618a18b1-dec3-4c4a-813b-988d9c065722]] and Sick of It All.

eras.title: Singers come and go
eras.text: Internal fights pushed Rob Fusco out right before a national tour. One King Down burned through two replacements, split, came back with Fusco, lost their drummer and finished as a four-piece, then skipped Hellfest and stopped.

years.h: Rob Fusco quits One King Down before the Earth Crisis tour
years.p: Internal conflict drives Rob Fusco out just before a national tour supporting Earth Crisis and [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]]. Ryan Downey of Burn It Down fills in for exactly two shows.
years.xp: Downey was never meant to stay. The band looked to Syracuse and found Jon Peters, who sang on their first full-length.

years.h: God Loves, Man Kills, sung by Syracuse's Jon Peters
years.p: One King Down's debut full-length, EVR 48, recorded at Max Trax Studios in Albany with Paul Benedetti. Punknews said it sounded like a different band altogether.
years.xp: Around this time guitarist Mike Scoville auditioned for the [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]]; Wikipedia says the job went to someone else. The band also shared a split CD with Spirit of Youth on Europe's Good Life Recordings in 1998.

years.h: Jon Peters leaves, One King Down split, Rob Fusco returns
years.p: After more touring Jon Peters quits and One King Down break up for a short time. When they re-form, Rob Fusco is back on vocals.
years.xp: A Punknews reviewer heard about Fusco's return from Equal Vision's Ian early in 2000, and was thrilled: Fusco, he wrote, sang in a metal-tinged hardcore band but still sounded human.

years.h: One King Down cover London Calling for a Clash tribute
years.p: One King Down's version of The Clash's London Calling appears on Chord Records' City Rockers: A Tribute to the Clash, next to [[Hot Water Music|c83907ee-8b5a-4547-8f68-96572243ea7f]], [[Dropkick Murphys|e8374874-4178-4869-b92e-fef6bf30dc04]] and [[Kid Dynamite|c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a]].

years.h: Gravity Wins Again: Rob Fusco's comeback record
years.p: One King Down's last Equal Vision release, EVR55, recorded at Max Trax in Albany with [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] on art direction. The CD adds the four Absolve songs.

years.h: Derrick Van Wie leaves; Matt Wood moves to One King Down's drums
years.p: Drummer Derrick Van Wie, still on Gravity Wins Again, departs. Guitarist Matt Wood moves behind the kit and One King Down carry on as a four-piece.
years.xp: Fusco told Lambgoat about watching Wood keep perfect time singing along to the radio while driving through a mountain tunnel, landing back in sync when the signal returned.

years.h: One King Down skip Syracuse Hellfest and call it quits
years.p: After skipping their slot at Hellfest in Syracuse, One King Down are done. Their last records are a split on When Angels Shed Their Wings Volume 2 and a three-way 7" with Mindsnare and Day of Contempt.

eras.title: Other bands, one lost demo
eras.text: With One King Down gone, Rob Fusco found a second home fronting a New York band, and the old band tried once to reconvene on tape. The record that mattered most got its anniversary reissue.

years.h: Rob Fusco becomes the singer of [[Most Precious Blood|1f43313f-4855-4b5f-af16-90ab6ab8cf36]]
years.p: Most Precious Blood, formed from the remains of Indecision, take on Rob Fusco when Tom Sheehan leaves to go back to school. Fusco fronts them on Trustkill records for years.

years.h: The unreleased Rob Loves, Man Kills demo
years.p: One King Down record a demo CDr whose title reworks their 1998 album around Rob Fusco's name. It stays unreleased.
Equal Vision reissues One King Down's Bloodlust Revenge on remastered vinyl. BrooklynVegan reported the physical copies sold out.

eras.title: Kids again at This Is Hardcore
eras.text: After seventeen years off, the Bloodlust line-up came back together, and One King Down ended up on bills with the bands they had once opened for.

years.h: One King Down return at This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia
years.p: Rob Fusco, the Scoville brothers, Matt Wood and Derrick Van Wie play This Is Hardcore, One King Down's first show in 17 years.

years.h: One King Down's first New York show in 17 years, in Clifton Park
years.p: One King Down headline Upstate Concert Hall in Clifton Park, outside Albany, with All Out War and Wisdom in Chains.
years.xp: The band posted after This Is Hardcore that they were still trying to process the weekend, and that it went far beyond anything they had hoped for.

years.h: One King Down open Earth Crisis's Firestorm shows, then tour Europe
years.p: One King Down support [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] at Firestorm 30th anniversary shows in Brooklyn, Cambridge, Syracuse and Amityville, then tour Europe in June with Shutdown and No Turning Back.

years.h: One King Down play For The Children Fest at LA's Belasco
years.p: One King Down play For The Children Fest at the Belasco Theater in Los Angeles.
